source_title_hint: The New, Better Way To Foam Roll
primary_summary: The video explains how to use a foam roller to manipulate femur position and improve hip internal rotation. It demonstrates two techniques: (1) placing the roller behind the femur and rolling down two‑thirds of the thigh to bias the femur into internal rotation, and (2) sitting on the roller with the sit‑bone contact to press the femur into internal rotation while gently leaning forward and back.

classification.usefulness_reason: Provides clear biomechanical rationale and step‑by‑step execution for a hip mobility technique.

problem_statements: Limited hip internal rotation can restrict functional movement and increase injury risk.
habits_or_contexts: People often use foam rollers only for muscle release and overlook their ability to influence bone position.
key_visual_points: Foam roller placed behind femur side
Sit‑bone contact while seated on roller
exercises_mentioned: Foam roller femur internal rotation roll
warnings_or_limitations: May feel tender; focus on bone repositioning rather than muscle pain.

knowledge_units.title: Foam Roller Femur Internal Rotation Roll
knowledge_units.summary: Roll a foam roller behind the femur from the top of the leg down about two‑thirds of the thigh to bias the femur into internal rotation and improve hip mobility.
observable_signs: Sensation of internal rotation of the femur
Mild tension in the hip/thigh region
mechanisms: Pressure applied behind the femur forces the femoral head into internal rotation within the hip socket
execution_steps: Place the foam roller on the side of the thigh with pressure behind the femur (≈19.4 s).
Start at the top of the leg and slowly roll down toward the knee, stopping about two‑thirds of the way (≈28.6 s).
Maintain straight leg without locking the knee; keep toes pointed upward (≈66.9 s).
Roll back up to the start point quickly (≈81.2 s).
cues: Move slowly and feel the bone shift
breathing_cues: Inhale as you roll down, exhale as you roll back up
when_useful: When hip internal rotation is limited
when_not_useful: If excessive joint pain is present
retest: Repeat weekly and assess range of internal rotation
advice: Focus on bone position; discomfort is normal but should not be sharp pain

knowledge_units.title: Sit‑Bone Foam Roller Internal Rotation Press
knowledge_units.summary: Sit on a foam roller with the sit‑bone in contact, cross the opposite leg, and gently roll forward to press the femur into internal rotation, using forward and backward leans to feel hip movement.
observable_signs: Feeling of femur being pushed into internal rotation
Gentle stretch in hip and thigh
mechanisms: Contact pressure on the sit‑bone transmits force to the femur, encouraging internal rotation within the hip socket
execution_steps: Sit on the foam roller with the sit‑bone on the roller (≈59.8 s).
Cross the opposite leg over the top leg; the straight leg is the side you want to improve (≈65.4 s).
Point the toes of the bottom leg gently upward (≈65.4 s).
Roll forward until you feel the greater trochanter, then back just behind it (≈62.6 s).
Lean forward slightly, feeling a stretch in the hip, then return to neutral (≈144.5 s).
Repeat the forward‑lean‑back motion while keeping the roller position (≈159.7 s).
breathing_cues: Inhale while leaning forward, exhale while returning
errors_to_avoid: Rolling too far down the thigh (avoid full knee‑to‑ankle range)
when_useful: When internal rotation is limited and you need a seated mobility cue
when_not_useful: If you have acute hip pain
retest: Assess hip internal rotation after each session
advice: Move only to tolerable stretch; focus on bone reposition rather than muscle pain
